title: Biological pathway models have more memory than structurally matched random networks

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Biological pathway models have more memory than structurally matched random networks

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Compared with 500 random gene-circuit networks matched to the biological models in size, edges, degree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness, the biological ODE pathway models show higher prevalence of most memory types, fewer no-memory cases, and more correlated memory types, indicating that generic network dynamics are not solely responsible for trainability.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Random networks do not show similar memory behavior as models of biological processes, indicating that generic network dynamics are not solely responsible for trainability.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “Abstract”. Scope: 35 BioModels pathway models versus 500 random synthetic gene-circuit ODE models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-02: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The numerical comparisons are explicit and can be rerun from public biological models and published random-network rules. The test resolves the stated model comparison, though not whether all generic network dynamics have been excluded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recreate the matched random-network ensemble and compare memory prevalence, no-memory frequency, and memory-type correlations with the 35 BioModels networks. Prespecified null distributions and effect statistics can confirm or refute each comparison.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Only 35 biological models represent a convenience sample.

Random-network results depend on ensemble-generation and matching choices.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.94
data existence: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prevalence contrast can be recomputed from public models and code. It does not cleanly show that generic network dynamics are uninvolved, because the null model is a different dynamical family matched only on a few structural summaries. The comparison tests a restricted version of the claim and leaves the evolutionary reading confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute memory-type prevalence, no-memory rates and cross-type correlations for the 35 biological models and for random ODE networks matched on the stated size and centrality measures. A higher biological prevalence on most types, with fewer no-memory cases and stronger correlations, would support the contrast; a matched or reversed pattern would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Random networks use a synthetic gene-circuit equation, while the biological set mixes protein and genetic models.

BioModels is a publication-biased sample, so enrichment need not mean selection for trainability.
